Poker Rules

Texas Hold'em with fixed bet steps: two cards of your own, five shared cards, and the best hand of five wins. Played with chips, which are only points.

The rules

The deal
Everyone starts with 200 chips. The dealer changes every hand. The two players after the dealer put in the blinds: 5 and 10 chips (with two players, the dealer puts in the 5). Then everyone gets two cards that only they can see.
Betting rounds
There is a betting round before the shared cards, then three shared cards are dealt (the flop) and another round follows, then a fourth card (the turn) and a fifth (the river), each with a betting round. The player after the dealer starts; before the flop, the player after the big blind.
What you can do
Fold: give up the hand. Check: go on without paying, if nobody has bet. Call: pay as much as the highest bet. Bet or raise: put in one fixed step more.
Fixed steps
A bet or raise is always one fixed step: 10 chips before the flop and on the flop, 20 chips on the turn and the river. In each round there can be at most 4 bets (a bet and 3 raises). There is no typing in of amounts.
All in
A player who cannot pay the whole amount puts in all their chips and is "all in". They can then win only as much from each other player as they put in themselves; the rest goes into a side pot for the others.
The showdown
If more than one player is left after the last round, the cards are shown. Each player makes the best hand of five cards from their two cards and the five shared cards. The best hand wins; equal hands share the pot.
The end
A player with no chips left is out. The game ends when you have no chips left or when you have all of them. A new hand starts only when you tap Next hand.

The hands

From best to worst. If two hands are of the same kind, the higher cards decide.

HandWhat it isExample
Royal flushAce, King, Queen, Jack and Ten of one suit.A K Q J 10
Straight flushFive cards in a row, all of one suit.9 8 7 6 5
Four of a kindFour cards of the same rank.Q Q Q Q 3
Full houseThree cards of one rank and two of another.8 8 8 K K
FlushFive cards of one suit, not in a row.K 10 7 4 2
StraightFive cards in a row, of mixed suits. The Ace can be high or low.9 8 7 6 5
Three of a kindThree cards of the same rank.7 7 7 K 2
Two pairTwo pairs of different ranks.J J 4 4 A
One pairTwo cards of the same rank.10 10 K 8 3
High cardNone of the above: the highest card counts.A Q 9 6 3

Who wins?

The shared cards are K♠ K♦ 7♣ 4♥ 2♠. With A♠ K♥ you have three of a kind (three kings). The computer's 7♦ 7♥ make a full house: three sevens and two kings. The full house wins.
